job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many people believe that muscles grow larger while you are lifting weights at the gym, but this is a common misunderstanding. In reality, exercise creates tiny tears in your muscle fibers, and the actual growth and repair process happens during your rest days, not during the workout itself. To support this growth, your body needs a balanced diet, but simply consuming excess protein powder without proper training will not magically build muscle. Another myth is that you must use expensive gym machines to build strength. You can effectively strengthen your muscles using your own body weight through exercises like push-ups or squats. Furthermore, some people think that if they stop exercising, their muscle tissue will transform into fat. This is biologically impossible; muscle and fat are two completely different types of tissue. If you stop being active, your muscles may shrink from lack of use, and you might gain fat if you continue to eat the same amount of calories, but one does not turn into the other. Finally, remember that sweating is just your body’s way of cooling down, not a direct measurement of how much fat you have burned. Consistent, balanced activity is the key to a healthy body.
response.summary: Muscles grow during rest periods rather than during the workout itself. Muscle and fat are distinct tissues that cannot transform into one another. Sweating is a cooling mechanism and not a direct indicator of fat loss.
